facts.raw_span: A woman in her 50s who was a never-smoker
presented with an enlarged, firm right ala
a lesion of the right nasal vestibule mucosa 5 years prior
biopsied and reported as a solid and cystic hidradenoma
p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative
recurrence of the lesion 8 months prior to presentation
the lesion was excised but recurred quickly after 2 months
tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
p63 positive and p16 negative, with positive margins
thicker right ala compared with the left ala
Downward papillomatous proliferation of small, uniform, slightly atypical keratinocytes within loose stroma
reflected ala after lateral rhinotomy showing tumor in ala and its extension into the floor of the nasal vestibule

concepts.why: The patient has a history of a solid and cystic hidradenoma that recurred after excision, with positive margins and p63 positivity.
The patient has a downward papillomatous proliferation of small, uniform, slightly atypical keratinocytes within loose stroma in the nasal vestibule floor and ala.
The patient has a solid and cystic hidradenoma with p63 positivity and p16 negativity, consistent with a sweat gland tumor.
The patient has an enlarged, firm right ala with a tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala.
The patient has a downward papillomatous proliferation of small, uniform, slightly atypical keratinocytes within loose stroma, consistent with a keratinocyte proliferation.

rationales.F02: Enlarged right ala suggests a tumor in the nasal ala.
rationales.F04: Biopsy report of solid and cystic hidradenoma supports the diagnosis of hidradenoma.
rationales.F05: p63 positive and p16 negative staining pattern is consistent with hidradenoma.
rationales.F08: Tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala suggests a tumor in the nasal ala or vestibule.
rationales.F09: p63 positive and p16 negative staining pattern with positive margins supports the diagnosis of recurrent hidradenoma.
rationales.F11: Downward papillomatous proliferation of small, uniform, slightly atypical keratinocytes is consistent with keratinocyte proliferation.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of a biopsied solid and cystic hidradenoma, recurrence of the lesion, and positive margins support the diagnosis of Recurrent Hidradenoma, with Nasal Vestibule Papillomatosis being a close runner-up due to the downward papillomatous proliferation of keratinocytes.
